## @langchain/langgraph@1.6.0

### Minor Changes

- [#3121](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3121)
[`dbfb9a5`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/dbfb9a5e93000b6a0e2ee27d428866a6ea006d36)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - fix(langgraph): give
messages and tools events the namespace of the graph that ran them
  
`messages` and `tools` stream events now carry the namespace of the
graph that ran them:
  
- An event's namespace no longer ends with the node that made the call.
Root tokens have the namespace `[]`, so with `subgraphs: true` they
stream as `messages`, not `messages|model:<id>`, and a subgraph's tokens
as `messages|sub:<id>`.
- Events from a model or tool called inside a `task()` belong to the
graph that called the task: they stream without `subgraphs: true`, under
that graph's namespace.
- Without `subgraphs: true`, events from inside subgraphs no longer
stream. A subgraph node's returned messages still stream, whole, when it
ends, and a node that streams its own subgraph with `streamMode:
"messages"` or `"tools"` still receives that subgraph's events.
- Messages sent with `pushMessage` follow the same rules, so a node that
streams its own subgraph receives the messages that subgraph pushes.
- Apps that show subagent messages as they stream, like `useStream` with
`filterSubagentMessages`, now need `streamSubgraphs: true` when they
submit, as they already did with a Python server.
  
  `streamEvents` with `version: "v3"` is unchanged.

### Patch Changes

- [#3119](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3119)
[`58d490e`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/58d490e07568621787a814ab7ce24e5da0cfe658)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - fix(langgraph): keep
every message a node returns in messages stream mode
  
- In `streamMode: "messages"`, the id-less messages a node returned all
got one id, and an id-less message could take the id of a sibling that
had one, so the messages reducer kept only one of them and the saved
state depended on the stream mode. Each id-less message of a node's
output now gets its own id.
- Messages a node returns through `Command({ update })` are now emitted
in `messages` mode, as in Python. So are all the messages of a list of
updates that holds a `Command`, such as `ToolNode` returns when one of
its tools returns a `Command`; before, none of that list's messages were
emitted, and they reached clients only with the next `values` event.
- A model tagged `nostream` still streams no tokens, but when its node
returns its message in a list with a `Command`, as `createAgent` does,
that message now streams whole when the node ends, as it already did for
a plain update and does in Python.
  
  `streamEvents` with `version: "v3"` is unchanged.

- [#3145](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3145)
[`5cf585b`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/5cf585bae6ed80488e59ff752f04390be3b9e6a8)
Thanks [@hntrl](https://github.com/hntrl)! - fix(langgraph): route a
RemoteGraph's subgraph events like a local graph's when it streams
inside a node
  
When a node streams a `RemoteGraph` and its parent graph is streamed
with `subgraphs: true`:
  
- The node no longer receives the remote graph's subgraph events unless
it passed `subgraphs: true` itself. With `streamMode: "updates"` it got
`["model", "child"]` where a local graph gives `["child"]`. `messages`
events are not filtered. The server sends each message once, from the
namespace where it first saw it, so it never sends the top-level copy
the node would get from a local graph, and filtering would leave the
node with no messages.
- The parent now receives the remote graph's subgraph events, at every
depth. Before, it received only the remote graph's top-level events.
- The same holds when the node passes `subgraphs: false`. Before, that
turned off subgraph events for the parent too. So a node that streams
with `streamMode: "messages"` and `subgraphs: false` now gets the
subgraph's message tokens instead of the whole message at the top level,
as it already did when it didn't pass `subgraphs`, and as Python's
`RemoteGraph` does.

- [#3127](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3127)
[`a3fe525`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/a3fe52505c82953c9636330ab2d1266d382366ec)
Thanks [@sera-wi](https://github.com/sera-wi)! - List a `ToolNode`'s
tool names under the `__tools` node metadata key in `getGraph()` and
`getGraphAsync()`, matching Python, so graph viewers such as Studio can
show which tools it runs.

- [#3118](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3118)
[`7ab1b8d`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/7ab1b8d840c068c2593fea4683899508d93e6b33)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - fix(langgraph): stop
reporting a paused tool as failed on the tools stream
  
A tool that calls `interrupt()`, or whose run is drained, no longer
emits `on_tool_error` on the `tools` stream mode. The tool is paused,
not failed: on resume it runs again and emits `on_tool_start` and
`on_tool_end`. `ToolNode` now re-throws a drain, as it already did an
interrupt, instead of turning it into an error `ToolMessage`.

## @langchain/langgraph-api@1.5.7

### Patch Changes

- [#3144](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3144)
[`e26cb84`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/e26cb846363dae6f4ae337d99a6340aba3673905)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - fix(langgraph-api):
cancel a stateless streamed run when its request drops and
`on_disconnect` is `cancel`
  
`POST /runs/stream` never cancelled its run when the client went away,
before or after the response started, because the stream only cancelled
runs it joined with a thread id. A stateless run created with
`on_disconnect: "cancel"` now stops when its request drops, as thread
runs already did, and `GET
/runs/:run_id/stream?cancel_on_disconnect=true` gets the same fix.
Cancelling a stateless run that has not started yet now deletes the run,
and its temporary thread when no other run is left on it, instead of
leaving an `interrupted` run and its thread behind. Runs created with
`on_disconnect: "continue"` keep running.

- [#3157](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3157)
[`844f6fc`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/844f6fcafc8ad1b0b56b69bec302e25968fb974d)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - The dev server's run
stream joins (`GET /threads/:thread_id/runs/:run_id/stream`, `GET
/runs/:run_id/stream`) now honor `stream_mode` as the Agent Server does,
so `client.runs.joinStream(..., { streamMode })` drops other modes'
events instead of returning all of the run's events. Errors always pass,
and either messages mode keeps both message formats. Joins without
`stream_mode` are unchanged.

- [#3151](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3151)
[`32542a5`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/32542a57e86fd55406eeaf08f850f6eaaf9a6583)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - A run created on a busy
thread without a `multitask_strategy` is now queued (`enqueue`), as on
the Agent Server and in the API reference, instead of being rejected
with 422.

- [#3143](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3143)
[`824f24c`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/824f24ced5ee5a6d1c60c66b52031d61c2f7f30e)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - Fix three bugs in the
legacy run stream:
  
- In `messages` mode, each chat model reply streams under one message
id. Anthropic sets the id only on a reply's first chunk, so
`messages/partial` could switch to a `run-<runId>` id mid-reply that
never matched the id in `messages/complete`.
- In `messages` mode with `stream_subgraphs: true`, `messages/complete`
is now sent for the root graph's messages. It was never sent before.
- With `stream_subgraphs: true`, a node that streams a runnable of its
own (for example a generator `RunnableLambda` called with the node's
config) no longer fails the run with `TypeError: rawTuple is not
iterable`, in any stream mode.

- [#3142](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3142)
[`3f21e26`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/3f21e26235f04e1181facccf11166720b082b185)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - Runs that were running
when the dev server restarted, for example on a hot reload after a file
save, are now retried when it starts again and continue from their last
checkpoint. Before, they stayed `running` forever, their thread stayed
busy and new runs on it were rejected with 422.

- [#3142](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3142)
[`3f21e26`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/3f21e26235f04e1181facccf11166720b082b185)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - The `rollback`
multitask strategy, and cancelling with `action=rollback`, now roll back

the run is cancelled, then deleted with its checkpoints, so the next run
starts from the state before it, and its stream ends without an error.
Before, the run ended as `error` and its writes stayed on the thread.

- [#3142](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3142)
[`3f21e26`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/3f21e26235f04e1181facccf11166720b082b185)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - Deleting a thread, or a
run, while the run is running no longer stops one of the server's run

enough of these, new runs were never picked up.

## @langchain/langgraph-sdk@1.12.9

### Patch Changes

[`e0109cb`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/e0109cb5711f42c8c4986a61967d2a7634a4ef0a)

framing, colonless fields, stream-leading BOM handling, and empty event
ID resets during reconnection. Match Python streaming behavior: empty
payloads yield null, events inherit the reconnect cursor, and
ID-only/retry-only blocks update internal state without being yielded to
callers. Cleared event IDs are exposed as undefined. Pending unnamed
data is flushed at EOF, matching Python's existing tolerant EOF
behavior.

[`b5f96bd`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/b5f96bdac43542a053a80cb4b056d710cf46393c)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - A run abandoned by

[`3aa46f1`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/3aa46f1075a7a2975461dc4b42f86867def9a139)

[`a181b4d`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/a181b4d95501a41b949e1f9f1dea9ed055a50147)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - With history enabled,

- [#3153](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3153)
[`5e7fa49`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/5e7fa49a0c3bfa3c68aff4e982483f098062ba8e)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - Joining a run from its
first event in a mount that already streamed it no longer doubles each
message's text, subagent messages included. A join that resumes from a
`lastEventId` still continues the message where it left off.

- [#3159](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3159)
[`204fc6f`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/204fc6fa7c5d6c427a2a85f6ec5c6219afac5efc)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - With history enabled,
`submit` in the `useStream` hook and `StreamOrchestrator` no longer pins
the run to the cached head of the shown branch when the latest branch is
shown, so turns added elsewhere since the history was read (another tab,
a cron, an API call, or this tab's own earlier run when a second submit
was queued behind it) stay on the shown branch instead of moving to a
sibling branch. A shown branch whose head is not the newest loaded
checkpoint still forks from that head.

- [#3140](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3140)
[`918f958`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/918f958768c69d952769fcb979844490b7b40ded)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - Without history, the
`useStream` hook and `StreamOrchestrator` now read the thread again
after a run that succeeds when the state shown had an interrupt, a node
still to run or a task error, so an answered approval no longer comes
back and an old error goes away. A run on a thread that showed none of
these makes no extra request, and a failed read reports no error. With
history, a failed read after a run no longer fails the run in the hook
or skips `onFinish` in `StreamOrchestrator`.

- [#3152](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3152)
[`3c632fa`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/3c632fa2aa2d7e35f2540f556d8318f157ebe306)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - A stream that
reconnects now gets a fresh set of reconnect attempts each time an event
arrives, as the Python SDK does, so a long stream no longer gives up at
its sixth drop when every reconnect worked. A frame with only an `id:`
or a `retry:` field does not count as an event.

- [#3124](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3124)
[`a73261d`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/a73261dd575f4a8a84058a241cd60ccabdb08ccf)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - `stop()` in the
`useStream` hook and `StreamOrchestrator` no longer loses the session.
Without history and without an `onFinish` that takes the thread state,
stopping a running stream put back the thread state read when the thread
opened, so the turns sent since disappeared and `onStop` edits were
overwritten. A stop now reads the thread and shows what the server kept,
with the `onStop` edits applied on top. With or without history, a stop
no longer shows the cancellation as an error, or the node it cut off as
a breakpoint.

- [#3123](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3123)
[`b5f96bd`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/b5f96bdac43542a053a80cb4b056d710cf46393c)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - After a reload, a
subagent delegated by an older turn is no longer shown with the tool
results of a newer turn.

- [#3123](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3123)
[`b5f96bd`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/b5f96bdac43542a053a80cb4b056d710cf46393c)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - After a reload, a
subagent that is still running or waiting on an approval no longer shows
the state of a regular tool called before it in the same message.

- [#3123](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3123)
[`b5f96bd`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/b5f96bdac43542a053a80cb4b056d710cf46393c)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - With `streamSubgraphs`,
values from a subgraph that is not a subagent no longer replace the root
state while the subgraph runs. Its results show once its node returns.

- [#3123](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3123)
[`b5f96bd`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/b5f96bdac43542a053a80cb4b056d710cf46393c)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - A numeric `throttle`
notifies at most once per interval while values keep changing, as
documented, instead of waiting until they stop.

- [#3137](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3137)
[`2965bc1`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/2965bc1083945c16f38cdc9ef427991d7af11ff6)
Thanks [@richardscarrott](https://github.com/richardscarrott)! -
fix(sdk): re-parse streamed tool call args at most every 50ms instead of
on every chunk
  
The `useStream` hook from `@langchain/langgraph-sdk/react` re-parsed a
streaming tool call's full arguments on every `messages` chunk, so the
work grew quadratically with the length of the arguments. It now reuses
the previous parse and re-parses at most every 50ms, and once more when
the stream ends. Subagent messages get the same treatment.
  
The `@langchain/core` peer dependency is raised from `^1.1.48` to
`^1.2.18`, the first release that parses tool call chunks lazily. Older
releases parse them on every chunk regardless, so they would get the
delay without the speedup.

`messages` and `tools` stream events now carry the namespace of the

Root tokens have the namespace `[]`, so with `subgraphs: true` they

stream. A subgraph node's returned messages still stream, whole, when it

"messages"` or `"tools"` still receives that subgraph's events.

streams its own subgraph receives the messages that subgraph pushes.
- Apps that show subagent messages as they stream, like `useStream` with

submit, as they already did with a Python server.

`POST /runs/stream` never cancelled its run when the client went away,

and its temporary thread when no other run is left on it, instead of
leaving an `interrupted` run and its thread behind. Runs created with
`on_disconnect: "continue"` keep running.

[`e0109cb`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/e0109cb5711f42c8c4986a61967d2a7634a4ef0a)

ID resets during reconnection. Match Python streaming behavior: empty
payloads yield null, events inherit the reconnect cursor, and
ID-only/retry-only blocks update internal state without being yielded to
callers. Cleared event IDs are exposed as undefined. Pending unnamed
data is flushed at EOF, matching Python's existing tolerant EOF
behavior.

Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - A run abandoned by
`clear()` or `stop()` no longer runs `onSuccess`, so a thread switch
during a reconnect backoff no longer loads the previous thread's
history.

- [#3158](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3158)

paused. Effects replayed by StrictMode, Fast Refresh or `<Activity>` no
longer run a pending headless tool twice in the hook, nor, under Fast

Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - With history enabled,
`joinStream` in the `useStream` hook and `StreamOrchestrator` now shows
the thread state read after the joined run ends, as `submit` already
does, instead of the joined stream's last values.

- [#3153](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3153)
[`5e7fa49`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/5e7fa49a0c3bfa3c68aff4e982483f098062ba8e)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - Joining a run from its
first event in a mount that already streamed it no longer doubles each
message's text, subagent messages included. A join that resumes from a
`lastEventId` still continues the message where it left off.

- [#3159](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3159)

Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - With history enabled,
`submit` in the `useStream` hook and `StreamOrchestrator` no longer pins
the run to the cached head of the shown branch when the latest branch is
shown, so turns added elsewhere since the history was read (another tab,
a cron, an API call, or this tab's own earlier run when a second submit
was queued behind it) stay on the shown branch instead of moving to a
sibling branch. A shown branch whose head is not the newest loaded
checkpoint still forks from that head.

- [#3140](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3140)
[`918f958`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/918f958768c69d952769fcb979844490b7b40ded)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - Without history, the
`useStream` hook and `StreamOrchestrator` now read the thread again
after a run that succeeds when the state shown had an interrupt, a node
still to run or a task error, so an answered approval no longer comes
back and an old error goes away. A run on a thread that showed none of
these makes no extra request, and a failed read reports no error. With
history, a failed read after a run no longer fails the run in the hook
or skips `onFinish` in `StreamOrchestrator`.

[`3c632fa`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/3c632fa2aa2d7e35f2540f556d8318f157ebe306)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - A stream that
reconnects now gets a fresh set of reconnect attempts each time an event
arrives, as the Python SDK does, so a long stream no longer gives up at
its sixth drop when every reconnect worked. A frame with only an `id:`
or a `retry:` field does not count as an event.

- [#3124](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3124)
[`a73261d`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/a73261dd575f4a8a84058a241cd60ccabdb08ccf)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - `stop()` in the
`useStream` hook and `StreamOrchestrator` no longer loses the session.
Without history and without an `onFinish` that takes the thread state,
stopping a running stream put back the thread state read when the thread
opened, so the turns sent since disappeared and `onStop` edits were
overwritten. A stop now reads the thread and shows what the server kept,
with the `onStop` edits applied on top. With or without history, a stop
no longer shows the cancellation as an error, or the node it cut off as
a breakpoint.

- [#3123](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3123)
[`b5f96bd`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/b5f96bdac43542a053a80cb4b056d710cf46393c)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - After a reload, a
subagent delegated by an older turn is no longer shown with the tool
results of a newer turn.

- [#3123](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3123)
[`b5f96bd`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/b5f96bdac43542a053a80cb4b056d710cf46393c)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - After a reload, a
subagent that is still running or waiting on an approval no longer shows
the state of a regular tool called before it in the same message.

- [#3123](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3123)
[`b5f96bd`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/b5f96bdac43542a053a80cb4b056d710cf46393c)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - With `streamSubgraphs`,
values from a subgraph that is not a subagent no longer replace the root
state while the subgraph runs. Its results show once its node returns.

- [#3123](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3123)
[`b5f96bd`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/b5f96bdac43542a053a80cb4b056d710cf46393c)
Thanks [@eliornl](https://github.com/eliornl)! - A numeric `throttle`
notifies at most once per interval while values keep changing, as
documented, instead of waiting until they stop.

- [#3137](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/pull/3137)
[`2965bc1`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/commit/2965bc1083945c16f38cdc9ef427991d7af11ff6)
Thanks [@richardscarrott](https://github.com/richardscarrott)! -
fix(sdk): re-parse streamed tool call args at most every 50ms instead of
on every chunk
  
The `useStream` hook from `@langchain/langgraph-sdk/react` re-parsed a
streaming tool call's full arguments on every `messages` chunk, so the
work grew quadratically with the length of the arguments. It now reuses
the previous parse and re-parses at most every 50ms, and once more when
the stream ends. Subagent messages get the same treatment.
  
The `@langchain/core` peer dependency is raised from `^1.1.48` to
`^1.2.18`, the first release that parses tool call chunks lazily. Older
releases parse them on every chunk regardless, so they would get the
delay without the speedup.
